backlog.spec: Before ranking, regress the raw measured values on log heavy-atom count (ordinary least squares, training molecules only) and take the residuals. Rank-normalize these residuals to (0,1) with the existing (rank-0.5)/n formula and use them as the SVR and ARD target. Predictions then rank molecules by their size-corrected clearance. Add the size term back to the ranks by blending 0.8 of the residual-rank score with 0.2 of the rank of the heavy-atom count, so that the final score still reflects size. Keep the kernels and blend weights unchanged.
backlog.title: Size-residualized rank target

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, after the existing clip-to-5 standardization of RDKit descriptors, fit PCA on the training descriptors only and keep components covering 95 percent of the variance. Whiten each component to unit variance (divide by sqrt of its eigenvalue), clip the whitened coordinates at plus or minus 5, and apply the same projection to test molecules. Use the whitened coordinates in the descriptor RBF kernel with gamma = 1/(number of retained components). Keep the 0.5/0.5 Tanimoto/RBF mix, SVR and ARD (fit on the original standardized descriptors) unchanged.
backlog.title: PCA-whitened descriptor RBF kernel

backlog.spec: Sort training molecules into 10 deciles of the rank-normalized target. For each of 8 seeded replicates, draw a 75 percent subsample stratified by decile and fit the SVR (same precomputed kernel rows, C=5, epsilon=0.05) on it. Predict the test set with every replicate and rank-average the predictions. Keep the ARD member fit once on all training data and the 0.7/0.3 rank blend unchanged. Stratification ensures every replicate sees the full range of clearance, which can reduce variance from unlucky subsamples without changing the model class.
backlog.title: Target-decile stratified SVR bagging

backlog.spec: Fit a RandomForestRegressor (200 trees, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=3, random_state=seed) on the Morgan bits using the rank-normalized training target. Define the proximity kernel as the fraction of trees in which two molecules fall in the same leaf: compute leaf indices with model.apply() for train and test, then K[i,j] = mean over trees of (leaf_i == leaf_j). Replace the 0.5/0.5 Tanimoto/descriptor-RBF mix with (Tanimoto + RBF + proximity)/3 for both K_train and K_test, keeping the same SVR (C=5, epsilon=0.05) and the same ARD member. Note the forest is fit only on the training fold, so there is no leakage.
backlog.title: Random-forest leaf-proximity kernel for the SVR

backlog.spec: Change how the two similarity kernels are combined. Currently K = 0.5*(Tanimoto + RBF_descriptor). Instead use the elementwise product K = Tanimoto * RBF_descriptor, which keeps a pair similar only when both fingerprint and physchem descriptors agree. Keep the same gamma = 1/n_descriptors, the same SVR (C=5, epsilon=0.05) and the same ARD blend. Compute K_train and K_test with the same formulas and the same clipping, so the only change is the operator.
backlog.title: Product kernel instead of additive kernel mix

backlog.spec: Before computing Morgan fingerprints, call Chem.AddHs on each parsed molecule so that hydrogen counts are part of the environment. Use the Morgan generator with an atom-invariant function that combines atomic number, formal charge, total H count, and aromaticity, at radius 2 and 2048 bits. Use the same binary bits, the same Tanimoto kernel, and the same SVR and ARD members. This adds hydrogen and charge information that the current heavy-atom-only invariants lack, and it does not add any new model component.
backlog.title: Explicit-hydrogen, charge-aware Morgan fingerprint

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, fit sklearn DictionaryLearning (n_components=40, alpha=1.0, transform_algorithm='lasso_lars', random_state=seed, max_iter kept small) on the training Morgan bit matrix only. Transform both train and test Morgan matrices into sparse code vectors and standardize them using training statistics. Append these codes to the standardized descriptor matrix before the descriptor RBF kernel. Leave the Tanimoto kernel and the ARD member unchanged apart from the extra columns. The goal is a learned low-dimensional basis for fingerprint structure, which differs from the NMF and PLS features already tried.
backlog.title: Sparse dictionary-learned codes of Morgan bits

backlog.spec: Replace the SVR solver with a simple first-order solve of kernel ridge in the dual: minimize 0.5*||K a - y||^2 + 0.5*lam*a^T K a with lam=0.3 on the standardized rank target. Run 1500 steps of full-batch gradient descent with step size 1/(lambda_max(K)+lam) estimated by power iteration (30 steps, seeded), and keep a running Polyak average of the iterates over the last half of the steps. Predict with K_test @ a_avg. This swaps the solver rather than the features, and it gives a different implicit regularization path from the SVR epsilon-tube. Keep the same kernel mix and the same ARD blend.
backlog.title: Polyak-averaged dual iterates for the kernel regression solve

backlog.spec: Add a LightGBM member trained on the Morgan bits concatenated with the standardized descriptors. Fit three LightGBM quantile regressors at alpha 0.3, 0.5, and 0.7 (learning_rate=0.03, 400 rounds, num_leaves=15, min_child_samples=20, feature_fraction=0.3, bagging_fraction=0.8, seed-controlled), and average their predictions to get a robust central estimate. Convert to ranks and blend as 0.6*SVR-rank + 0.25*ARD-rank + 0.15*LGB-rank. Keep the total run time well under 10 minutes for 15 fits by limiting rounds. The quantile averaging is a form of regularization against outlier targets, which the squared-error members do not have.
backlog.title: Quantile-averaged LightGBM as a small-weight blend member

backlog.spec: Make the kernel mixing weight a function of training progress instead of a constant. Build the SVR as a short sequence of three fits with the same C=5 and epsilon=0.05. Stage 1 uses K = 0.8*Tanimoto + 0.2*RBF, stage 2 uses 0.5/0.5, and stage 3 uses 0.2*Tanimoto + 0.8*RBF. Each stage's fitted dual coefficients are used as the warm start for the next stage in the sense that the stage-3 predictions are averaged with the stage-1 predictions in rank space. Final SVR rank score = mean of the three stage ranks. This is a curriculum that begins with the fingerprint similarity and ends with the physchem similarity.
backlog.title: Scheduled decay of the Tanimoto weight in the kernel mix

backlog.spec: Run stability selection on the standardized RDKit descriptors. Draw 50 random 70% subsamples of the training molecules (seeded from the seed argument). On each subsample compute absolute Spearman correlation of each descriptor with the rank-normalized target, and keep the top 25 descriptors. Count how often each descriptor is selected and keep those selected in at least 60% of subsamples. Build the descriptor RBF kernel and the ARD member only on that stable subset, with gamma = 1/(number kept). Apply the same kernel mix and blend weights as the incumbent. The selection is done inside fit_predict on training data only.
backlog.title: Stability-selected descriptor subset before the RBF kernel

backlog.spec: Fit the SVR on the same kernel mix at a ladder of regularization strengths C in {0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10}, in increasing order. Each fit is a separate SVR object, but reuse the same precomputed kernel matrices so no kernel is recomputed. Take the final prediction as the mean of the five rank-normalized predictions. This is a different use of the C grid than the averaging already tried, because the ladder shares the Gram matrix across all five fits and keeps the test-time cost low. Keep the ARD member and the 0.7/0.3 rank blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Warm-started C ladder for the SVR

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, split the training molecules into 4 scaffold-grouped inner folds using the Murcko scaffold of each training molecule (group by scaffold SMILES, seeded assignment of groups). For each inner fold, fit the SVR and ARD members on the other folds and compute Spearman correlation of each member's predictions with the true rank-normalized target on the held-out fold. Choose the SVR weight w from the grid {0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9} that maximizes mean inner Spearman of w*SVR_rank + (1-w)*ARD_rank. Then fit both members on all training molecules and blend with the chosen w. The blend is tuned to the same scaffold-grouped shift the harness evaluates on.
backlog.title: Pseudo-Spearman-driven blend weight from inner scaffold folds

incumbent.description: Add an ARDRegression (default priors, max_iter=300) on the standardized, clipped RDKit descriptors, fit to the rank-normalized target, and output 0.7 times the SVR test-set rank plus 0.3 times the ARD test-set rank.

memo: Helped: changing model family (random forest 0.6103 to LightGBM 0.5726 to Tanimoto-kernel SVR 0.5491), rank-normalizing the target (0.5310/0.5307), averaging the Tanimoto kernel with a descriptor RBF kernel (0.4830), and adding ARDRegression on clipped standardized descriptors (0.4736/0.4644; incumbent 0.4690). Did not help: FCFP 0.5877, MACCS 0.5421, stacking 0.5558, MLP 0.5500, RankSVM 0.5957, Laplacian solve 0.5716, quantile descriptors 0.5470. Most later tweaks (extra kernels, SVR ensembles, sample weights, SMARTS blocks, target encodings) stayed within noise (sd 0.0070) or got worse. Timeouts: ElasticNetCV, Gaussian process, neural network; keep jobs well under the limit. Next: tune the ARD/SVR blend weight and SVR gamma. Combine ARD with the Gobbi kernel (0.4680/0.4791) or the ridge prior (0.4711/0.4728). Try the ErG+MQN features (0.4643) alongside ARD. Try other cheap Bayesian linear models on descriptors.
